note: HAND-MAINTAINED. Defects in the *reference compiler* that this suite has observed and cannot itself falsify. An oracle-derived suite inherits the reference's bugs by construction, so the only honest response to finding one is to record it where consumers can read it -- not to normalise it away into an expectation that quietly makes the bug the specification. Every entry carries a runnable reproducer and a declarative assertion, so `validateDefects` re-checks at the current pin whether the defect still manifests. An entry that stops reproducing fails the build: that is upstream fixing it, and the entry must then be closed rather than left to rot. Entries also expire; see docs/DEFECTS.md for why that gate is time-based and what it costs.

entries.title: Predicate.ParamUntyped is dead by assignment in Parser2.param()
entries.summary: Parser2.param() initialises `var kind` to TreeKind.Predicate.ParamUntyped, then overwrites it with TreeKind.Predicate.Param three lines later with no branch in between. close(mark, kind) therefore always receives Predicate.Param, and Predicate.ParamUntyped can never appear in any tree from any input. Weeder2 still pattern-matches on ParamUntyped in two places, so the producer and the consumer of this kind disagree about whether it can occur -- which is what makes this a defect rather than a retired kind. Searched upstream at this pin: flix/flix has no issue or pull request matching ParamUntyped, Predicate.Param, untyped predicate parameter, or dead assignment, so this is unreported. Two open items sit in the neighbourhood without touching it -- flix/flix#13389 revises predicate weeder errors and its diff contains no ParamUntyped, and flix/flix#13033 proposes removing PickException from Weeder2 and discusses the predicate code. That second one means upstream is already working in this file, which is the argument for reporting this as a small deletion rather than as a bug: nothing misbehaves, and the whole of the defect is a dead store plus two match arms in Weeder2 that can never be reached. A review-ready upstream draft is staged at https://github.com/wstein/flix-fork/issues/5, with a standalone minimal reproduction at https://github.com/wstein/flix-repro-predicate-paramuntyped -- a flix-template project pinned by digest to v0.77.0, so it needs only a JDK.
entries.impact: A parser that reproduces the reference's intent rather than its behaviour would emit Predicate.ParamUntyped for an untyped predicate parameter and be reported as divergent. The reference is the oracle here, so agreeing with the bug is what conformance requires; this entry exists so that requirement is visible rather than silently inherited.

entries.title: Weeder2 crashes on a math-name operator used infix
entries.summary: Parser2 has a dedicated binary operator for math-symbol names: peekBinaryOp maps TokenKind.NameMath to BinaryOp.NameMath (Parser2.scala:1675), NameMath is a member of FIRST_BINARY_OP (Parser2.scala:1703), and it carries its own precedence. So `a ⊆ b` lexes and parses cleanly into Expr.Binary with the symbol closed as Operator. Weeder2.visitBinaryExpr then matches the operator token against a fixed set -- the keyword operators, the literal cases, ColonColon, ColonColonTight, Tick and GenericOperator (Weeder2.scala:1244) -- which omits NameMath, and falls through to `throw InternalCompilerException("Expr.Binary operator not recognized")` (Weeder2.scala:1248). The two phases disagree about whether NameMath is an operator, which is what makes this a defect rather than unsupported syntax. Confirmed against the released v0.77.0 jar from the command line, which prints the compiler's own bug-report banner, not only by driving the phases directly. Upstream has seen this exception before, from a different trigger: flix/flix#13320 reported it for a keyword used as an infix function name (`1 `checked_cast` 2`), and flix/flix#13326 fixed that path on 2026-09-19 by adding a Tick case to the same match. That fix is an ancestor of the pinned v0.77.0 commit and does not touch NameMath, so this path survives it. A search of flix/flix issues and pull requests for the exception text, for NameMath, and for math-operator crashes finds nothing covering this trigger, so it is unreported as of this pin. A review-ready upstream draft is staged at https://github.com/wstein/flix-fork/issues/4, with a standalone minimal reproduction at https://github.com/wstein/flix-repro-namemath-infix-crash -- a flix-template project pinned by digest to v0.77.0, so it needs only a JDK.
entries.impact: Nothing for a parser: the reference's own parser accepts the input and produces the tree this repository publishes, so a consumer that agrees with fixtures/expected is correct. It is recorded because the fixture expressions__math-name-operator.flix asserts a tree the reference cannot actually compile, and a reader is entitled to know that the suite's authority stops at the parse. It also bounds what a positive fixture means here.
